newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major to decide on single currency when issues clear.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major to decide on single currency when issues clear.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Monday that Britain would decide on whether to join a single European currency when it was clear about the issues involved.

"We will make our decision when we are clear about all the necessary issues including, crucially, our assessment of the prospect for real and sustained economic convergence," Major told Parliament in a statement on last weekend's EU summit in Dublin.

Major said he expected Britain to meet the required economic conditions for joining the single currency. However, he said: "Although we expect to meet the required economic conditions, we have the right to decide whether or not we want to join, if it goes ahead."
Also he reiterated his doubts about whether enough EU member states would be in a position to join.

"I have made no secret of my doubts about whether enough countries will be sufficiently convergent to allow a single currency to go ahead safely on the present timetable. I repeated these doubts in Dublin."

He added: "It is important that the figures themselves are not fudged. But, whether or not particular countries meet particular targets on a particular day is less important than the extent of genuine readiness for such a far-reaching step."
